question:
A mathematics class models a quadratic expression as $P(t)=x+yt+zt^2$, where $x$, $y$, and $z$ are unknown constants. Three observed values are $P(0)=2$, $P(1)=6$, and $P(2)=16$. These observations produce a system of three linear equations that can be solved by writing it in matrix form and finding the inverse of its coefficient matrix. The resulting expression is then used to predict another value.

(a) Form the three equations and write them as $AX=B$.

(b) Evaluate $|A|$ and determine whether the coefficients are uniquely determined.

(c) Find $A^{-1}$ and hence determine $x$, $y$, and $z$.

(d) Calculate $P(3)$ and verify the three original observations.
explanation:
(a)
Using $P(t)=x+yt+zt^2$,
$$P(0)=x=2$$
$$P(1)=x+y+z=6$$
$$P(2)=x+2y+4z=16$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\\16\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
Let
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\2 & 4\end{vmatrix}=4-2=2$$
Since $|A|\neq0$, the system has a unique solution and the coefficients are uniquely determined.

(c)
The inverse of $A$ is
$$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\-\frac{3}{2} & 2 & -\frac{1}{2}\\\frac{1}{2} & -1 & \frac{1}{2}\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\\16\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-3+12-8\\1-6+8\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$x=2,\quad y=1,\quad z=3$$
Thus,
$$P(t)=2+t+3t^2$$

(d)
$$P(3)=2+3+3(3^2)=5+27=32$$
Verification:
$$P(0)=2$$
$$P(1)=2+1+3=6$$
$$P(2)=2+2+3(4)=16$$
Thus, all the observations are verified, and $P(3)=32$.

options.A:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&1\\1&2&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\\16\end{bmatrix}$
(b) $|A|=2$, so the coefficients are unique
(c) $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\-\frac32&2&-\frac12\\\frac12&-1&\frac12\end{bmatrix}$ and $(x,y,z)=(2,1,3)$
(d) $P(3)=32$, and all three observations are satisfied
options.B:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&1\\1&2&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\\16\end{bmatrix}$
(b) $|A|=0$, so the coefficients are not unique
(c) $(x,y,z)=(2,3,1)$
(d) $P(3)=20$
options.C:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&1\\1&2&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\\16\end{bmatrix}$
(b) $|A|=4$
(c) $(x,y,z)=(2,3,1)$
(d) $P(3)=20$, while only the first two observations are satisfied
options.D:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&1\\1&2&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\\16\end{bmatrix}$
(b) $|A|=2$
(c) $(x,y,z)=(2,1,3)$
(d) $P(3)=30$, although the original observations remain satisfied
